summary.headline: Oswal Pumps FY26 operating income hit record INR2,064 crore (+44.3%) and PAT INR376 crore (+34.1%), but FY27 guidance is back-ended with H1 at risk.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income rose 39.8% YoY to INR510 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR118 crore (23.2% margin) and PAT of INR93 crore (+44.8%). Full-year operating EBITDA margin was 24.9%, and Q4 margin moderated sequentially on competitive tender pricing and input-cost pressure from geopolitical tensions. Operating cash flow turned positive in Q4 (INR171 crore), though FY26 was still negative at INR77 crore before a INR116 crore Maharashtra receipt on April 2. Management guided FY27 growth of 20-25%, with H1 likely to see a moderate decline and growth back-ended on the PM-KUSUM 2.0 rollout, plus FY27 operating EBITDA margin of 22-23%.

negative INR77 crore (FY25: negative INR142 crore)

segments.name: Solar pumps (PM-KUSUM and state schemes)
segments.commentary: Executable order book of 19,912 pumps as of May 15, 2026, plus a near-term pipeline above 25,000 pumps; cumulative 1,06,122 systems executed across 15 states. Management said the order book covers Q1 and roughly part of Q2.

segments.name: Solar modules, rooftop, utility and C&I
segments.commentary: Entered rooftop via first order under PM Surya Ghar; SPV Oswal Doon Baran Bundi Solar Projects (60% stake, HAM model, Rajasthan state buildings). Combined pipeline about 300 MW across rooftop, utility and C&I; management expects about INR1,000 crore of business from these lines in FY27 (ballpark).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY; medium-term growth of 30-40% thereafter.
H1 FY27 expected to see a moderate but temporary revenue decline; management said the order book covers the prior year's revenue but it is being conservative given new-segment execution risk.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 22.0-23.0%; PAT margin guided at 15-16%. Management said margins should improve beyond FY27 as operating leverage builds and input costs normalise.
Execution under PM-KUSUM 2.0 expected from Q3 FY27 (November onward), assuming a June announcement; LOIs assumed by end-September.
FY27 capex of about INR350 crore to be infused; IPO-funded capex (about INR90 crore at parent for pump/motor capacity and automation) to complete by Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Solar module capacity: first phase of 1 GW expansion by Q1 FY27; remaining 0.5 GW by Q3 FY27.
Oswal Solar capacity to rise from existing 600 MW to 2.1 GW, with backward integration (aluminium extrusion, EVA).
Pump and motor capacity expansion and automation at parent to complete by Q3 FY27; management said capex is on track, with possible 2-4 month slippage in infrastructure works.
Management said pump capacity rises about 2.25x and module capacity 2.5-3x; combined capacity could support about INR6,000-6,500 crore top line without further expansion (per management on call).
Inverter production: assembly to start in the coming months, with end-to-end in-house production targeted within 6-7 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects PM-KUSUM 2.0 to be announced around June 2026 and said demand indications were strong; no timing was firmly committed.
Tender pricing remains competitive as new entrants bid aggressively; management hopes PM-KUSUM 2.0 tenders will reflect higher input costs.

Receivables: MSEDCL (Maharashtra) was the main customer in FY26; delays linked to state elections, a Guinness-record project and third-party funding (AIIB) timing. Management said routine receivable cycle is 150-160 days (90% in 120 days, balance in next 120).
Repaid INR311 crore of debt from IPO proceeds at about 8.5-9% cost; INR200 crore general corporate purpose fund fully used in working capital.

qa_highlights.question: How much H1 FY27 decline is expected, and is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk if PM-KUSUM 2.0 is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book can cover last year's revenue, but it is being conservative on H1 given new-segment execution risk; H1 may be flat or decline, and Q3-Q4 would make up for it.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is expected in rooftop solar versus the core business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not prioritising profitability in the first phase and is focused on execution learnings; it expects margins to be achieved over time given backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise and which states are delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays mainly to MSEDCL in Maharashtra (elections, a Guinness-record project, AIIB funding timing); Q4 saw large payments. It expects receivable days to fall 30-40 days under PM-KUSUM 2.0 modifications.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from PM-KUSUM 2.0 announcement to order and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: If announced in June, tenders by August, LOIs by end-September, and execution from November (Q3) per management.

qa_highlights.question: Inverter entry: competition and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inverters are for internal backward integration and not a standalone sales model; assembly first, with in-house end-to-end production in 6-7 months.

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue from non-pump lines (rooftop, PM Surya Ghar, modules, inverter)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR1,000 crore from these lines in FY27 (ballpark), while acknowledging the segments are new and uncertain.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 announcement timing; any delay pushes order inflow and Q3 execution.
Receivable days at 155 (CFO) or 152 days; cash conversion cycle of 172 days and negative FY26 operating cash flow before the April 2 receipt.
Margin pressure from geopolitical input-cost increases and competitive tendering; FY27 margin guidance of 22-23% sits below FY26's 24.9%.
Execution risk and unproven margins in new rooftop, C&I, utility and inverter businesses.
Dependence on Maharashtra (MSEDCL) and government-backed payers for receivables.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and PM-KUSUM 2.0, but notably cautious on H1 FY27 visibility and margins, repeatedly describing near-term pressure as transitionary. Several answers were loose or drifted from the questions asked, and some figures (receivable days, the cumulative pump count, capacity-based top line) were stated inconsistently.
key_quotes: So, if we look at FY25, our cash flow was negative by around INR152 crores, which by December 2025, the cash flow was negative by around INR247 crores.
Basically, we expect 90% payment in 120 days and after that, the 10% payment is in the next 120 days.
But quarter-on-quarter, I feel myself that I should walk conservatively in H1 this year to give you visibility.
